title: Breathless at 3 a.m. on the respiratory ward
summary: A 68-year-old with known lung disease is more breathless and drowsy than at handover.

evidence.claim: NIV indicated for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure in COPD with pH < 7.35 and PaCO2 > 45 mmHg after initial medical therapy
evidence.source: Rochwerg B, et al. Official ERS/ATS clinical practice guidelines: noninvasive ventilation for acute respiratory failure. Eur Respir J 2017;50:1602426

evidence.claim: Repeat blood gas within 1-2 hours of starting NIV; failure to improve pH and RR by 4 hours should prompt escalation decision
evidence.source: Davidson AC, et al. BTS/ICS guideline for the ventilatory management of acute hypercapnic respiratory failure in adults. Thorax 2016;71 Suppl 2:ii1-35

evidence.claim: Target SpO2 88-92% in patients at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure
evidence.source: O'Driscoll BR, et al. BTS guideline for oxygen use in adults in healthcare and emergency settings. Thorax 2017;72 Suppl 1:ii1-90

patient.presentingStory: Admitted yesterday with a COPD exacerbation. Nurse calls because he is more drowsy and his oxygen was turned up to 4 L/min an hour ago for SpO2 85%. Now on nasal cannula 2 L/min after the nurse turned it back down.
patient.history: COPD (FEV1 38% predicted), ex-smoker 50 pack-years, home oxygen not prescribed. Lives with wife, walks 50 m on the flat. No treatment limits documented.

orderEffects.note: No meaningful effect within the case window; included so the order is realistic

actions.reason: Intubated. The debrief reviews whether NIV was given a fair trial first.

findings.examine: Drowsy but rousable, speaking in short phrases. RR 28, accessory muscle use, pursed lips. Widespread expiratory wheeze, prolonged expiration, hyperinflated chest. No asterixis. Warm peripheries.
findings.cxr: Hyperinflated lungs with flattened diaphragms. No consolidation, no pneumothorax, no effusion.

then.detail: SpO2 above 96% for 20+ minutes in a patient at risk of hypercapnia (target 88-92%).

then.text: He's more awake and asking for a cup of tea.

then.reason: pH and work of breathing improving on NIV.

then.text: He's barely responding to voice now.
Doctor, he's tiring and getting drowsy. Can you come and look?
He's breathing more slowly and looks more settled. I'll keep an eye on him.

predictionPoints.question: You have just changed his support. Over the next hour, which way will each of these go?
predictionPoints.explanation: Pressure support above EPAP adds tidal volume and offloads tired muscles. Alveolar ventilation rises, so PaCO2 falls and pH rises; as work of breathing eases, RR usually falls. If you changed to HFNC or a mask instead, the response depends on the device, which is why the engine marks this rather than a fixed key.

predictionPoints.question: On BiPAP, which setting mainly lowers PaCO2?
options: The difference between IPAP and EPAP
predictionPoints.answerKey: The difference between IPAP and EPAP
predictionPoints.explanation: The IPAP-EPAP difference is the pressure support that generates extra tidal volume. EPAP mainly helps oxygenation, splints the upper airway and offsets intrinsic PEEP.

rubric.description: Started NIV for acute hypercapnic acidosis
Repeated the blood gas within 2 hours of starting
Kept SpO2 in the 88-92% target range (no prolonged over-oxygenation)

keyPoints: pH below 7.35 with a raised PaCO2 after initial treatment is the trigger for NIV in a COPD exacerbation.
Pressure support (IPAP minus EPAP) drives CO2 clearance; EPAP helps oxygenation and offsets intrinsic PEEP.
Hypoxaemia in COPD is driven predominantly by ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) mismatch rather than true anatomical shunt, making it readily responsive to modest supplemental oxygen.

Target SpO2 88-92%. Excessive oxygen worsens hypercapnia through three mechanisms: reversal of hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction worsening V/Q mismatch, the Haldane effect shifting CO2 off deoxygenated haemoglobin, and a fall in minute ventilation (Aubier 1980; West 12e).
Re-check the gas within 1-2 hours. No improvement in pH and RR by about 4 hours means deciding on escalation.
